papers.title: Micropore‐Forming Gelatin Methacryloyl (GelMA) Bioink Toolbox 2.0: Designable Tunability and Adaptability for 3D Bioprinting Applications
papers.abstract: It is well-known that tissue engineering scaffolds that feature highly interconnected and size-adjustable micropores are oftentimes desired to promote cellular viability, motility, and functions. Unfortunately, the ability of precise control over the microporous structures within bioinks in a cytocompatible manner for applications in 3D bioprinting is generally lacking, until a method of micropore-forming bioink based on gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) was reported recently. This bioink took advantage of the unique aqueous two-phase emulsion (ATPE) system, where poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) droplets are utilized as the porogen. Considering the limitations associated with this very initial demonstration, this article has furthered the understanding of the micropore-forming GelMA bioinks by conducting a systematic investigation into the additional GelMA types (porcine and fish, different methacryloyl-modification degrees) and porogen types (PEO, poly(vinyl alcohol), and dextran), as well as the effects of the porogen concentrations and molecular weights on the properties of the GelMA-based ATPE bioink system. This article exemplifies not only the significantly wider range of micropore sizes achievable and better emulsion stability, but also the improved suitability for both extrusion and digital light processing bioprinting with favorable cellular responses.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该项研究仅集中于生物墨水的材料特性与成型工艺，完全未涉及人工智能或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper contains no AI/ML integration, no computational modeling, and no autonomous decision-making; it is purely a materials characterization study.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发可精确控制微孔结构的生物墨水以提升细胞功能。
summary_zh.method: 系统研究不同类型明胶甲基丙烯酰与致孔剂对微孔成型性能的影响。
summary_zh.result: 实现了更宽的微孔尺寸范围和更好的乳液稳定性，适用于挤出和数字光处理生物打印。
summary_zh.validation: 通过细胞实验评估生物相容性及打印适用性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop bioinks with precisely controllable microporous structures for enhanced cell viability and function in 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Systematic investigation of various gelatin methacryloyl types and porogens (PEO, PVA, dextran) to tune micropore formation and emulsion properties.
summary_en.result: Achieved a wider range of micropore sizes and improved emulsion stability, with suitability for both extrusion and digital light processing bioprinting.
summary_en.validation: Cytocompatibility and printability were validated through in vitro cell culture and printing tests.
